title: deliverable (Work/<spoke>/deliverables/<name>.md) lifecycle contract
description: Thin lifecycle-only contract for durable, human/agent-authored deliverables under the Work/ surface — the durable + human-authored quadrant the binder, library, and workshop do not fill. Deliverables are heterogeneous (a brief, a deck-source, a memo, and a multi-page report share no body shape), so this contract governs frontmatter and lifecycle ONLY: it carries no body-structure and no length governance, leaving the body free-form. The frontmatter type registration (type: deliverable) lives in governance/frontmatter-rules.json#types.deliverable; this contract carries the lifecycle enums (status, audience) and the audit-time placement signal. Enforcement fires at BOTH layers: write-time on REGISTERED-spoke Work/ writes — the pre-write-guard.sh remap prelude rewrites a registered Work/<spoke>/ write onto the vault path BEFORE the 3-tier schema block, so the write IS governed — with the librarian suite over the Work/ symlink view as the audit-time backstop for everything else (unregistered spokes, hand-authored files reached via the scoped symlink walk). A deliverable is never machine-written. Note the bounded exception: foundation capabilities DO machine-write generated, sentinel-bounded files into the work root (the auto-maintained work-side directory map and the work-subfolder _index.md navigation files, each carrying a generated sentinel). Those generated surfaces are NOT deliverables and are out of this contract's scope; they are disjoint from the deliverable class, so the never-machine-written boundary for human/agent-authored deliverables is unchanged.

_design_notes.consumer: skills/librarian audit suite (index-maintain / placement-validate / frontmatter-enforce / xref-check) covers Work/** at audit-time via a scoped invocation (--scope <vault>/Work) — the whole-vault walk does not recurse into the Work/ symlink, so deliverables are reached the same way library-index reaches the _library root. Write-time governance ALSO fires on a REGISTERED-spoke Work/ write: the pre-write-guard.sh remap prelude rewrites the registered Work/<spoke>/ path onto the vault view BEFORE the 3-tier block, so the write is governed; the librarian audit-time pass is the backstop for unregistered spokes and hand-authored files. A deliverable is never machine-written. The work root is not write-untouched, however: foundation capabilities machine-write generated, sentinel-bounded files into it (the auto-maintained work-side directory map and the work-subfolder _index.md navigation files). Those generated surfaces are a disjoint artifact class — not deliverables — and are out of this contract's scope; the deliverable surface (human/agent-authored README/updates and the deliverable files themselves) stays never machine-written.
_design_notes.thin_contract_note: Models the minimal-viable file-type stub shape (frontmatter + lifecycle, free-form body), NOT the rich library-article body-structure shape — deliverables are too heterogeneous for a single body contract. Per-deliverable-kind structure governance is an archetype subtype layered via overlay-master.json, not part of this base contract.
_design_notes.evolution_protocol: R-37 atomic lockstep — this runtime artifact + governance/frontmatter-rules.json#types.deliverable (the type registration) + governance/foundation-master.json forward-composed move in one commit.

routing: A markdown file under the Work/ surface that declares type: deliverable in its frontmatter activates this contract. Placement under Work/** is an audit-time placement advisory (the type's expected_path), not the write-time trigger; write-time governance fires instead via the pre-write-guard.sh registered-spoke remap prelude, which rewrites a registered Work/<spoke>/ write onto the vault path so the 3-tier schema block governs it.

frontmatter._note: The real required[] enforcement surface is governance/frontmatter-rules.json#types.deliverable; this block mirrors the universal typed cohort + its value-typing for legibility. Value-typing is enforced write-time by the pre-write-guard.sh property-type format regex (R-64).

contract_rationale: A deliverable is durable, project-scoped work product the author owns and edits across its lifecycle, so the contract governs only the lifecycle frontmatter and leaves the body free-form; deliverables are too varied in shape for one body-structure to fit, and per-kind structure belongs to an archetype subtype rather than the universal base.
audience_rationale: The base audience values stay internal and external so the universal vocabulary remains archetype-neutral; a narrower refinement of the external value is an overlay subtype an adopter adds for their own publish tooling, not a base value the foundation ships.
